Asked what a browser, or a script, sending resume repeatedly does to an unpaid call. Each failed resume reset the unpaid limit, so asking every few minutes kept the call and its Live session open forever (LM1); and every resume was a ledger write under a wallet lock, so a burst of them was a burst of writes (LM2).
A resume while paid charges nothing; a call pressed long before Live answered is charged for the time since the press.
The start gate already refuses a voice call without billing; the live route now refuses it too, so neither door carries a call free.

Looked for other ways to hold an unpaid call: hanging up ends it; a paused call's Live session still rotates and resumes as before; the pause limit is the only thing that ends an abandoned one, which is what LM1 protects.
The paused flag crosses goroutines as an atomic; the timers and the minute count are touched only by the relay's loop. All relay tests pass under -race.

A capture that fails after a reservation is refunded; that minute's operation is then refunded, so it cannot be charged again and the call stays paused until its limit. Chosen deliberately: a ledger fault must never become a free minute.
A call that ends while paused leaves no held credits: a refused reservation writes nothing.
